palette.notes: Uses the author's own Mondo palette; the method blocks each body part in a distinct flat colour first and adds final colour only after the motion works.

lighting: Not covered; studies are flat-colour blocking first, shading last.
silhouette: Simple designs on purpose: detail makes clean motion harder. Wings get marked joints so they fold at clear points instead of bending like rubber.

motion.timing: The bird flap uses 8 frames (stated as matching the other studies; fewer can work). No per-frame durations given.
principles: secondary motion layered last (head, tail, body bob)
opposing up-down motion of hips and shoulders

texture: None during animation: flat colour blocks per body part, texture and feathers added once the cycle reads.
camera: Static side and front views; the cycles loop in place.

acting.enters: Not covered; cycles loop on the spot.
acting.acts: Character comes from the gait: a child marching vs an elderly shuffle on the same rig. Animate one part across all frames at a time (legs, then arms, head, body).
acting.depth: Front and side views of the same flyer; no staging in depth.

techniques: colour-code each body part so it can be tracked frame to frame
animate one part across the whole cycle before the next
quadruped = two biped leg pairs, back leg one step behind the opposite front leg
front and back legs cover the same distance or the body accordions
hips and shoulders bob in opposite, equal amounts
mark wing joints to avoid rubbery bends
add the overall body bob last
feel: simple flat shapes + extremes first + body bob layered last = a loop that reads cleanly before any detail
for_fred: Build Fred's swim loop like the wing study: two extremes of the tail, smear in-betweens, and the whole-body bob added last, with a marked joint where the tail bends. Give Pixie a distinct walk personality (a prowl, not a generic trot) instead of adding more animations.
